subject: Mutual action plan: Solstice Health capacity & lock-in timeline
messages:
From: Alex Rao <alex@solsticehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Solstice MAP ask: evaluation -> production capacity planning

Jonas —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Solstice Health is excited to move from proof-of-concept to a limited production pilot. We want to capture a simple mutual action plan that locks in capacity and timelines so our engineering and procurement teams can align. High level asks: 

- Evaluation window: 6 weeks (pilot with PII-safe data subset) starting Jan 10 2027
- Target production: early Feb 2027 (soft launch) with full rollout by end of Q1 2027
- Need lead time / procurement requirements for: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) options
- Initial GPU sizing: we estimate ~6–12 concurrent streams at 2k tokens average. Can you advise H100 vs A100 tranches and recommended reserve sizes?
- Pricing/commitment: rough order of magnitude for 3-month and 12-month reservation tiers

Also can you provide any standard MAP template you use (milestones, acceptance criteria, SOC2 checklist) so we can run it against our vendor intake? CC'ing procurement.

Appreciate a short MAP draft and a proposed lock-in date window.

—Alex
Alex Rao
Head of AI Platforms, Solstice Health
alex@solsticehealth.com
+1 415-555-0196

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rao <alex@solsticehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Solstice MAP ask: evaluation -> production capacity planning

Alex — thanks, great next steps. I put together a compact MAP and attached two stubs: Solstice_MAP_draft.xlsx (milestones / owners / acceptance criteria) and H100_pool_sizing.pdf (sizing scenarios). Quick summary below so procurement and engineering can triage this quickly.

Proposed MAP highlights:
- Evaluation (Jan 10 — Feb 20): pilot with synthetic + redacted PII subset; acceptance = <15% hallucination rate on clinical templates + latency SLOs met for 95th perc.
- Lock-in window: target reservation decision by 2026-12-22 (allowing hardware allocation before Jan staging).
- Tranche options (initial, scale):
  * Option A (conservative): Reserve 8x H100 (1st month) -> increase to 24x H100 within 8–12 weeks if acceptance met
  * Option B (lower cost, more routing): Reserve 12x A100 + Redwood-hosted higher-capacity fallbacks for peak bursts
- Lead times (guideline): Dedicated (reserved capacity in our US regions): 8–12 weeks to guarantee H100 tranche availability; Private on-prem (customer-managed): typically 12–16 weeks depending on procurement / site readiness + KMS/HSM setup
- Autoscaling & fallbacks: we recommend a policy with a fixed reserved minimum + burst pool (on-demand) and automatic routing to smaller quantized variants if mem pressure occurs.
- Security/compliance gating: SOC 2 Type II evidence, network diagrams, and an ATO checklist — see MAP sheet.

Next actions (proposed):
1) Procurement: review the MAP workbook and confirm the desired tranche option (A or B) and target lock-in date.
2) Eng (Karthik/Irene): review performance targets and confirm runtime tuning tasks for Jan test harness.
3) Legal/Procurement: we'll push a reservation term quote + DocuSign link once tranche is selected.

If Dec 22 is tight for you, we can accept a Dec 31 lock-in with a scaled staging plan, but earlier gives better chance of H100 availability for Jan test runs.

Attaching the two files as placeholders — I'll update the workbook with estimated monthly costs in the next 48 hours.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
(650) 555-0124

Attachments: Solstice_MAP_draft.xlsx (spreadsheet), H100_pool_sizing.pdf (pdf)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Solstice MAP ask: evaluation -> production capacity planning

Jonas / Irene — quick internal notes to include in the MAP before we send to procurement: 

- Kernel / model decisions: recommend starting evaluation on a 70B dense model quantized to 4-bit for latency; fallback family should be a 30B low-latency quantized variant for bursts.
- Pool sizing recommendation (engineering POV):
  * Pilot tranche: 8x H100 (shared across 6–8 concurrent streams, headroom for KV caching)
  * Production ramp (0–90 days): scale to 16–24x H100 depending on QPS growth. Use incremental tranches (8 + 8) to shorten lead time risk.
- Lead time reality check: procurement-to-deployment for Dedicated H100 pools in us-west2: 8–12 weeks if we can lock and ship from partner inventory; if customer elects Private on-prem, add 4–6 weeks for rack + networking + KMS integration.
- Acceptance gating: we need a 3-point smoke test for each tranche: 1) steady-state latency under target load, 2) KV/prefix cache hit rate >40% for common prompts, 3) model quality regression <5% vs POC baseline.
- Cost mitigation: recommend a blended contract: baseline reserved capacity to meet min SLOs + explicit burst budget (on-demand) for unexpected spikes.

I'll take the action to update the MAP with the engineering appendix and a short checklist for procurement (requirements: signed SOW/reservation, billing contact, POC IP sanction).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@solsticehealth.com>

Cc: Alex Rao <alex@solsticehealth.com>, procurement@solsticehealth.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Solstice MAP ask: evaluation -> production capacity planning

Jonas — thanks for the draft MAP and the sizing guidance. Procurement has reviewed the high-level options and we prefer Option A (H100 tranche) for latency predictability. A couple of asks from our side: 

- Can you send a DocuSign reservation quote for the 8x H100 initial tranche (3-month and 12-month pricing lanes) plus an option to add two additional 8x tranches?
- We need the SOC2 evidence bundle and the network diagram (redacted ok) for our vendor intake form.
- Procurement will target a lock-in decision by 2026-12-22; can you confirm Redwood can commit to H100 allocation if we sign by that date?

I'll attach our PO template for your legal/procurement team to review. Let's schedule a 30-minute MAP kickoff this week — Alex and I are available Wed 11/25 10:00–11:30 PT or Thu 11/26 14:00–15:00 PT. Please send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Procurement Manager, Solstice Health
maya.patel@solsticehealth.com
